title_clean: Coronavirus Lockdown Extension Effect on Stock Market
summary: PM announced a further 19-day lockdown. Argues the move was 90% expected, so already priced; SGX Nifty traded ~200 points above the India close; herd put-buyers set up for a premium collapse even if prices fell.
lessons: Markets can absorb good or bad news but not uncertainty; once an outcome is known, clarity itself re-prices risk.
When 90% expect a fall, the fall is already priced - consensus trades usually fail.
Option buyers can be right on direction and still lose when uncertainty resolves and premiums collapse.

strategies.adjustments: Exited or rolled by expiry; profit disclosed in a later review video
strategies.risks: Losses if the market breaks below the sold strikes; premium is the cap on profit

title_clean: Cash Secured Put for High Income
summary: Teaches the cash-secured put end to end: sell a put at a strike you are happy to own, collect premium, take delivery if assigned. Shows live positions (Bajaj Finance, IndusInd, Nifty puts) and a claimed Rs.45 lakh FY21 profit in three weeks.
lessons: Sell puts only at prices where you are happy to take delivery - the premium is income, the strike is your target entry.
Far-month puts pay large premiums and give delivery intent when the market reaches your buy zone.
Squaring off and buying in the open market is usually cleaner than waiting for physical settlement.

strategies.name: Cash Secured Put
strategies.construction: Sell a put at the strike where you want to own the stock; keep the full cash ready for delivery
strategies.numbers: Bajaj Finance 1800PE sold at Rs.100 (2 lots, Rs.50,000 collected); Nifty Apr 7500PE ~Rs.57; Dec-2020 6000PE ~Rs.200; ~Rs.19 lakh premium collected; claimed Rs.45 lakh FY21 P&L in 3 weeks
strategies.best_regime: Sideways-to-up markets, or when you want a lower entry price in a quality stock
strategies.adjustments: Square off the put and buy shares in the open market instead of physical delivery; exit any time before expiry
strategies.risks: Profit capped at premium; stock can fall far below strike; requires full cash backing of the strike

summary: Replies to ROI/margin critics by showing scale: ~23 lakh quantity through one broker in a day, about 1.5% of the 8700PE contract's day volume; argues absolute profit and capital-handling skill matter more than percentage ROI.
lessons: Absolute profit matters more than ROI percentage - the real skill is the amount of capital you can handle.

All charges are computed on premium, so selling low-premium options keeps costs proportionally tiny.

title_clean: How Gold Impacts the Stock Market
summary: Historical framing of gold: price fixed by UK for a century, market data from 1973; three spikes - 1980 Iran revolution/oil crisis, 2008 Lehman, 2020 COVID. Logic: global crisis forces rate cuts, money exits deposits into gold.
lessons: Gold spikes when a global crisis forces central banks to slash rates - near-zero deposit rates make yieldless gold attractive.
Whether to buy gold depends on your view of how long the crisis and the low-rate regime will last.

summary: Pre-results Infosys structure: short straddle at 650, converted to an iron fly with long 720CE/580PE wings, wings financed by selling double quantity of 750CE and 550PE. Payoff: max ~Rs.3.58 lakh (15%) at 650, protection zones 710/590.
lessons: Enter earnings trades the day before results and exit once the event resolves; hold further only with a stop-loss.
Finance protective wings by selling double quantity of farther strikes so the hedge costs nothing from pocket.
A naked short straddle is high risk; the same view becomes limited-risk when converted to an iron fly.

title_clean: Proof That Experts' Stock Recommendations Are Useless
summary: Builds the case that expert stock-picking barely beats chance: hundreds of coexisting technical methods cannot all work; Malkiel's blindfolded-monkey argument; WSJ dartboard contest (61% expert pick wins, only 51% beat the Dow); 2018 rerun where dart picks returned 17.3% vs experts -4.4% vs S&P +11%.
lessons: If hundreds of technical methods coexist, most cannot work - treat technical analysis as one input, never the system.
In the WSJ decade-long dartboard contest, pros beat the darts 61% of the time but beat the Dow only 51% of the time.
Public picks suffer an announcement effect; experts also skew to high-risk names - both flatter their track records.

title_clean: IndusInd Bank Earnings Trade - Strategy in Advance
summary: Contrasts results timing and IV: Infosys declares after hours (ATM IV ~67) while IndusInd declares intraday (ATM IV ~140). Plan: sell May-series 400CE+400PE straddle, hedge with current-month 500CE/300PE; net ~Rs.94.55/share (Rs.37,800/lot) on ~Rs.60,000 margin.
lessons: For high-IV stocks, sell the next-month straddle - richer premium with relatively smaller risk - and hedge with current-month wings.
Results timing matters: after-hours declarations carry gap risk, intraday declarations let you react.
ATM IV doubling between a quiet IT major and a volatile bank shows why event trades must be sized by IV, not by price.
